eindtekst: Pick tables, ask questions in plain language, and the Analyst answers with SQL that runs against your DuckDB workspace, powered by the remote or local model you configured in Settings.

stappen.tekst: The Analyst starts by scoping: every table in the workspace appears as a card with its field and row counts. Pick which ones the AI may look at.
Select all, deselect all, or click cards one by one. The Filter tables box narrows the list when the workspace grows.
The selected card is highlighted and the footer button comes alive: Analyze 1 table. This selection becomes the chat context.
Analyze opens the chat with the selected tables in context.

A clean start: the welcome screen names the tables in context and offers starter questions. Answers stream as text plus SQL, and every query lands in the results panel. (This demo runs without a live LLM key, so the chat stays in its honest empty state.)
Type a question in plain language. Enter sends, Shift+Enter adds a new line.
stappen.text: Give me an overview of the superstore data

stappen.tekst: The send button lights up. With a working API key this question would stream an answer with SQL that runs against superstore. Not sending it here: the demo key is fake, and an honest empty chat beats a staged reply.
What answers your questions is set in Settings: Remote API is the default, pointing at a chat completions endpoint with a model identifier.
Prefer no cloud at all? Local AI switches the Analyst to llama.cpp models that run on your own device.
The local picker lists downloadable llama.cpp models in Fast and Balanced tiers, sized for your RAM, with disk usage per model. Download one and the Analyst chats fully offline.
